resources.string: Short answers to get you going. Everything here works offline.

Self Watch keeps your body, activity and food in one place, on this phone only.

1. Fill in Me › Profile and Me › Goals, so calories and targets fit you.
2. Pair your watch on Devices.
3. Log a meal or a weigh-in with the + button.

Small steps count. Check in once a day and the trends do the rest.

Open Devices and tap Pair watch. Allow Nearby devices when Android asks, then pick your watch from the list.\n\nKeep the watch close, awake and charged. If it does not show up, open the phone settings on the watch and choose to pair a phone, then try again.

Once paired, the watch syncs by itself whenever it is near your phone. Tap Sync now on Body or Devices to sync straight away.\n\nFrom the watch come steps, heart rate, resting heart rate, sleep, stress, HRV, SpO2, intensity minutes and workouts with their GPS tracks. Devices › Data so far shows what has arrived.

Body, Activity and Food are stacks of cards. Tap a card to open its detail.\n\nUse ⋮ › Edit cards to show, hide and reorder cards, or start from a set that fits your main goal. Changes are saved at once.

Tap + on Body or Food.

• Search food: type a name and tap the food.
• Scan barcode: point the camera at the pack.
• Quick add calories: when you only know the number.

Recent foods are one tap away. The food database is optional; add it on Me › Food data. If you do not track food, turn it off in Settings.

Me › Data brings your history in from export files and watch files (FIT, GPX, TCX), and exports your data as CSV, JSON or a full Self Watch backup.\n\nTurn on automatic backup to a folder you choose, so a new phone is never a fresh start. Activity › ⋮ › Export activities saves your workouts as GPX, FIT or TCX.
Your data stays on this phone. No account, no ads, no analytics.\n\nMe › Privacy center gives every internet feature its own switch, and Network activity lists every request the app has made.

• Watch not found, or it will not connect: another watch app on this phone may be connected to it. Only one app can talk to the watch at a time, so close or disable the other app, then try again.
• Bluetooth must be on. On Android 11 and older, Location must be on too while you pair.
• Syncing stops in the background: set Self Watch's battery use to Unrestricted (App info › Battery).
• Still stuck: turn Bluetooth off and on, restart the watch, or remove the watch on Devices and pair again.

Open an issue on the Self Watch project page on GitHub. Say what you did, what you expected and which phone and watch you use.\n\nMe › About › Export logs saves the app\'s log to attach; debug builds also have Devices › Debug for Bluetooth captures. Logs hold no health values, but read them before you share. Report security problems privately, not in a public issue.
Most connection problems are fixed in a minute. Try these in order.
